title: Suspected non-accidental injury
stem: Paediatric area. Kylie, 16 months, has been brought by her father with burns to both feet. He says an older sibling put her in the bath 12 hours ago. Take a history from the father and explain your plan.

phases.title: History
phases.goal: A careful, non-judgemental history, noted word for word.

phases.title: Examine
phases.goal: The burns and the whole child, with a chaperone.

phases.title: Plan
phases.goal: Protect her, document, investigate, report, her brother; tell her father honestly.

review.text: Date of the new law. Your notes say Cap. 650 takes full effect on 1 January 2026. The Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse Ordinance came into force on 20 January 2026.

notes:
Checked against Hong Kong's Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse Ordinance (Cap. 650, in force 20 January 2026), the Social Welfare Department 'Protecting Children from Maltreatment — Procedural Guide', the Protection of Children and Juveniles Ordinance (Cap. 213), and NICE CG89 (Child maltreatment).

Red flags: delay in presentation, a history inconsistent with the injury or the child's development, changing stories, injury in a non-mobile child, patterns (symmetrical 'glove and stocking' immersion scalds with sharp tide-marks and sparing of flexures; cigarette burns; bruises on the ears, neck, buttocks, or with patterns; multiple fractures of different ages, metaphyseal and posterior rib fractures), other injuries, repeated attendances. Take a careful, non-judgemental history, document verbatim with times, examine fully (with a chaperone), photograph with consent, protect the child (admit as a place of safety), and involve the senior and paediatric team. Investigations: skeletal survey, CT head (under 1 year or with neurological signs), bloods (FBC, clotting, bone profile), ophthalmology for retinal haemorrhages; consider siblings.

Under Cap. 650 (from 20 January 2026) medical practitioners are mandated reporters: report serious child abuse to the Social Welfare Department or police as soon as practicable through the reporting platform. Your notes say Cap. 650 takes full effect on 1 January 2026; it came into force on 20 January 2026. The rest of your notes (FCPSU, 24-hour SWD hotline, admission under Cap. 213 section 34F if parents refuse) matches.

Perfect script checked against RCPCH child protection guidance and the HK Cap. 650 ordinance, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed the accusing and discharge options. Added an honest explanation to the father.

steps.label: History
steps.hint: Non-judgemental: what happened, when, who was there, delay, development, household, previous injuries.

Injury.t: Can you tell me exactly what happened?
Injury.tz: 你可唔可以話我知，究竟發生咩事？
Injury.rz: 佢阿哥，佢六歲，自己放水沖涼，將佢放咗入浴缸。佢尖叫。
Injury.r: Her brother, he's 6, ran the bath and put her in. She screamed.
Injury.mark: Open, non-judgemental questions about the event

Injury.t: When was this, and when did you notice the burns?
Injury.tz: 幾時發生？你幾時發覺佢燙傷？
Injury.rz: 琴晚大概八點。我以為會自己好返。
Injury.r: Last night, about 8. I thought it would heal.

Injury.t: Where were you? Who else was home?
Injury.tz: 嗰陣你喺邊？仲有邊個喺屋企？
Injury.rz: 我喺廚房。我女朋友出咗街。
Injury.r: I was in the kitchen. My girlfriend was out.

Injury.t: Can she stand or climb into a bath herself?
Injury.tz: 佢自己識唔識企，或者爬入浴缸？
Injury.rz: 佢啱啱先識扶住傢俬行。
Injury.r: She's just started walking holding on to furniture.

Household.t: Who lives at home and who looks after her?
Household.tz: 屋企有邊個住？邊個照顧佢？
Household.rz: 我、我女朋友、佢阿哥。我女朋友唔係佢阿媽。
Household.r: Me, my girlfriend, her brother. My girlfriend isn't her mum.

Household.t: Any previous injuries or hospital visits?
Household.tz: 佢以前有冇受過傷，或者入過醫院？
Household.rz: 三個月前斷過手——喺梳化跌落嚟。
Household.r: She broke her arm 3 months ago — fell off the sofa.

Household.t: Is everything OK at home? Does anyone feel unsafe?
Household.tz: 屋企一切還好嗎？有冇人覺得唔安全？
Household.rz: 最近壓力好大。錢方面有問題。
Household.mark: Screens for domestic stress and violence

steps.label: Examine (with a chaperone)
steps.hint: Burn pattern, other injuries head to toe, fontanelle, eyes, growth.

Burns.t: With a chaperone: look at both feet
Burns.r: Symmetrical burns to both feet up to the ankles with a sharp straight edge; soles spared; no splash marks. "An immersion, stocking pattern: it doesn't fit the story."

Other.t: A full skin examination, head to toe
Other.r: Fingertip-shaped bruises on the upper arms.
Other.mark: Examines fully and finds other injuries

Other.t: Fontanelle, eyes and her growth chart
Other.r: Fontanelle soft. Weight on the 3rd centile.

steps.label: Plan
steps.hint: Safety, senior and paediatrics, document, photos, investigations, report (Cap. 650), siblings.

opts.t: Admit her as a place of safety; inform my senior and the paediatric team
opts.mark: Keeps the child safe and escalates

opts.t: Document exactly what was said, with times; body map and photographs with consent
Skeletal survey, CT head, FBC, clotting, bone profile, ophthalmology
Mandatory report to the Social Welfare Department or police under Cap. 650; the hospital child protection coordinator
Consider the safety of her brother

steps.label: Talk to her father
steps.hint: Honest, non-judgemental: the burns, admission, and that others will be involved.

opts.t: Kylie's burns are deep and need treatment in hospital. The pattern of the burns worries me, so, as we must for any child with injuries like this, I'm going to involve the paediatric team and the social welfare services. We'll do some tests to check for other injuries.
opts.tz: Kylie 嘅燙傷好深，要留院治療。啲燙傷嘅形狀令我有啲擔心，所以，好似處理任何有呢類傷勢嘅小朋友一樣，我會通知兒科同社會福利署。我哋亦會做啲檢查，睇吓有冇其他傷。
opts.r: Are you saying I hurt her?

qs.q: Fracture highly specific for abuse in infants?

qs.q: Which investigation in a child under 2 with suspected abuse?

qs.q: Parents demand discharge; you suspect abuse. You…
qs.a: Contact SWD/police; the law allows holding the child
wrong: Let them go, then refer to social work by letter next week
Sedate the child so they cannot leave
Ask them to return tomorrow for review

badge.name: Safeguard
badge.flavor: Story versus injury versus development. Protect, document, report.

cards.q: HK Cap. 650 requires medical practitioners to…
options: Report serious child abuse as soon as practicable
Report only if the parents agree
Report within 30 days, after discussion with the family

cards.q: Bruising in a non-mobile infant is…

options: Sharp tide-marks, symmetry, sparing of flexures
A single small burn on the palm

cards.q: Retinal haemorrhages with subdural haematoma in an infant suggest…
Documentation in suspected NAI should be…
options: Verbatim, timed, with a body map
A brief summary at the end of the shift
Written up later from memory at home
A minor injury in an infant preceding serious abuse
A major burn in a toddler
A sports injury in a school child
